subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: What trusted/untrusted SKILL.md instruction boundary, capability metadata, enforcement scope, and compatibility rollout should OpenClaw adopt?
rationale: This changes the security boundary between model-visible skill instructions, system prompts, tools, memory, and existing skill workflows, so automation should not choose the permanent policy or migration behavior.

options.title: Approve Phased Core Isolation
options.body: Start with a maintainer-approved design for skill instruction precedence and capability metadata, then implement prompt/read-path enforcement, runtime tool/memory checks, tests, and docs in staged PRs.

options.title: Narrow To Scanning And Manifests
options.body: Treat Markdown scanning and inspect-only capability manifests as interim hardening while leaving stronger runtime isolation for a later RFC.

options.title: Keep Policy External
options.body: Rely on governance plugins and ClawHub review for this class of risk, and narrow or close the core item if maintainers do not want a core enforcement boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Core Isolation
recommendation.body: Start with a maintainer-approved design for skill instruction precedence and capability metadata, then implement prompt/read-path enforcement, runtime tool/memory checks, tests, and docs in staged PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current discussion signal and recent adjacent history across prompt, skills, and security-boundary policy.
